memos.scout:
The honest case for buying JOI now is weak, and I'd recommend skipping it.

What's genuinely positive: the curve looks organic. Bundle share is 1.3%, top-3 holder share is 6.8%, and it has 701 buyers with the completer holding only 26%. It's alive at 30 minutes, and graduation was not instant.

But the recent tape argues against demand holding. Over the last 15 minutes, sellers (512) outnumbered buyers (501), sell SOL (259) exceeded buy SOL (223), and price fell 54%. The coin is 78% below its 30-minute high. Post-graduation, the sell-to-buy ratio is 0.80, and a launch bot was present. Pool depth of 87 SOL means a $20 ticket moves the price, and the round trip costs 1.4-5.1% before any move.

The one reading in favor is that a 78% drawdown on a clean holder distribution could be a flush that finds a floor. But nothing in the brief shows buyers stepping in at these levels: net flow is negative and the most recent window is pure distribution. Waiting for net-positive flow over several minutes would be a better entry signal than what exists now.

Verdict: no buy. The case for demand persisting for the next 30-60 minutes is not supported by the data.

Post-graduation, sell-to-buy was 0.80 with 166 SOL of non-agent buys, so early demand has already been absorbed by exits.

Our $20 ticket plus ~1.4-5.1% round-trip costs and 30-second latency means we would be buying into a falling knife with a fat bid-ask gap and little reason to expect a bounce. Dead-cat bounces on coins down this far rarely clear fees. Skip.
